newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea Metals - Imports trimmed by falling won.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea Metals - Imports trimmed by falling won.

text.p: The sharply falling won has forced major South Korean trading houses to reduce base metal imports due to fears of huge foreign exchange losses, metal traders said on Thursday.
"We have no choice but to reduce (our) trade volume if we want to avoid sharp currency losses," a dealer with a major trading house in Korea said.
The won fell to a fresh seven-year low on Thursday of 894.20 to the dollar on expectations of rising demand for the U.S. unit, despite dogged intervention by the Bank of Korea.
The customs-cleared trade deficit rose to US$23.72 billion in 1996 from a $10.06 billion shortfall in the previous year.
South Korea's major export industries have been battered by the collapse of Hanbo Steel and Sammi Steel following almost four weeks of strikes by workers in January.
Aluminium import premiums for spot delivery were seen flat in a range between $85-$90 a tonne CIF Pusan over LME cash prices, traders said.
Domestic aluminium prices rose to 1.52 million won a tonne this week from 1.51 million last week, while copper prices were seen flat at 2.297 million won a tonne over the past week.
Domestic zinc prices were also flat at 1.187 million won a tonne the past week while lead prices were unchanged at 703,000 won a tonne.
Traders said the Office of Supply (OSROK) bought 2,550 tonnes of aluminium in tenders last Thursday.
They said the OSROK's purchase prices have been a benchmark on the domestic market.

The OSROK bought 1,285 tonnes of aluminium from LG Metals Corp at 1.525 million won a tonne for delivery to its Inchon warehouse and 530 tonnes at 1.52 million won a tonne for delivery to its Pusan warehouse, they said.
Taihan Sugar Corp also sold 560 tonnes at 1.528 million won per tonne for delivery to the OSROK's Taegu warehouse and 175 tonnes at 1.512 million won a tonne for delivery to the warehouse in Kwangju.
